summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of gold's performance and taxation in India, though some tax details are outdated or slightly inaccurate based on recent changes.

claims.claim: This rally pushed spot gold to $4,397 an ounce, though it remains below its January all-time high.
claims.note: Spot gold reached $4397 an ounce in August, and the all-time high was $5602 in January 2026.

claims.claim: While this is a robust performance, it's important to note that gold's current price remains below its all-time high of $5,602 an ounce recorded in January.
claims.note: The all-time high for gold was indeed $5,602 an ounce, recorded in January 2026.

claims.claim: Short-term capital gains (if held for less than 3 years) are added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.
claims.note: For physical gold and digital gold, the holding period for short-term capital gains is less than 24 months for transfers made on or after July 23, 2024. For Gold ETFs, it's less than 12 months.

claims.claim: Long-term capital gains (if held for more than 3 years) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.
claims.note: For physical gold and digital gold, the holding period for long-term capital gains is more than 24 months for transfers made on or after July 23, 2024, and is taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefits. For Gold ETFs, it's more than 12 months and taxed at 12.5% without indexation.

claims.claim: Sovereign Gold Bonds have specific tax benefits if held till maturity.
claims.note: Capital gains arising on redemption of SGB to an individual are exempt if held till maturity.

claims.claim: SGBs are government securities denominated in grams of gold. They are substitutes for holding physical gold, offering interest payments and capital appreciation linked to gold prices. They are issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India.
claims.note: SGBs are indeed government securities issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government of India, denominated in grams of gold, offering interest and linked to gold prices.

claims.claim: If you're looking to invest in gold digitally, explore the current series of Sovereign Gold Bonds issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
claims.note: The Sovereign Gold Bond scheme was discontinued in 2024 due to being an expensive method of borrowing for the government, and no new series have been issued after February 2024.
